proof.criterion: Review finding 3 fixed: the queue keeps a room whose rows will come due - a note during its step re-queues it, and a check that finds young rows comes back when they are due - so the 16-row / 15-minute bound is the queue's, not the hourly sweep's.
proof.surface: envoy-dispatch built from d741863c, real process on Postgres 16.2, DISPATCH_NATS_DISABLED=1, HTTP API
proof.observed: scenE: an upload every 3 s for 330 s (101 uploads). The rows older than 2 minutes reached 16 at most and were folded back to 1-5 while appends kept noting the room. After the writes stopped, they folded at idle +45 s and +120 s, which left 4 rows (the fold point and 3 rows not yet 15 minutes old). The final text is exactly version 101. scenF: 5 rows written at 01:06:08 and no more writes. They stayed 5 rows through +870 s and were 1 row at +900 s (01:21:11). The process had swept that hour at its start, before the writes, so no sweep folded them.
proof.negativeControl: In scenF the queue's first check, at +2 minutes, found 4 rows after the first, fewer than 16, so not due, and did not fold them. They stayed 5 rows until the 15-minute rule made them due.

proof.criterion: Review finding 2 fixed: buffered folds are bounded (bufferedFolds = 4) and loads beyond the bound wait and complete.
